a.text: Life itself is a sort of profound horror.
You don't know where it's going to take you. Even worse, even when there aren't thirty-some-odd siblings and hundreds of other relatives clamoring to make your decisions for you––
You still sometimes find yourself under attack, out of nowhere. Such as, uh... right now.
There are no think tanks, no 'there's no way this could be wrong because everyone believes it,' only a bandit pulling up with a crossbow and the sand kicking up as hard as he drives.

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Um, I... don't think we can pass through Windy Beach. That place is Catastrophe central. Each year, up to seventy thousand trucks are damaged or destroyed when passing through...

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: But, that's not the point. Our transport's already pretty beat up...

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: A-Also, you should take a look at this. In addition to Catastrophes, there are other factors that can worsen the damage to a vehicle...

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Originium fuel leakage, transmission failure leading to secondary incidents, explosions in close proximity to mining sites... So we'll want to steer clear of the mines

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Hey, are you listening?

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: That's right, Potlid. Climb up from here, saw off the branch, then connect the hose to the top of the tree!

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: The saw... is so heavy...

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: But it's okay... the ankle braces Lanns gave me are very secure. Just imagine that you're a big tree musbeast, use the braces to hold onto the tree, and jump up with a 'whoosh'...

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: ...I know I can do this, and make everyone happy.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Huh...? My back feels lighter all of a sudden?

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Oi, jacker. I didn't tell you to do that.

steps.name: Ray
steps.text: Sure. You didn't tell me to do anything. But, I have experience collecting water from bottletrees.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Okay, so you have a heart after all. But I still need you to return Potlid's tools.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: After all, I certainly trust my old partner a whole lot more than I trust the random jacker.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Heehee...

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Besides, it's not like we're really trying to become a bottletree water delivery truck.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: We just need to put on enough of a disguise before entering the city that nobody can tell it's an intercity transport that's gone off route.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Slap some decoration on as well –– don't let anyone see that the ol' girl's been punched full of holes before being patched over with sheet metal.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Potlid, let's go over our cover story with the jacker here.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Okay.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: If anyone asks, tell them we're transporting this bottletree, and the water in the trunk's gotta be bucketed up for transport into the factory. As for the tree branch decorations on the vehicle, it's just a little something the boss enjoys.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: That's right. Bulletproof cover story, if I do say so myself.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Haha, never would've imagined that these bottletrees would be saving our hides when we're running from Catastrophes on our long 'detour'.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Whoever decided to plant these bottletrees in the middle of nowhere, thank you.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: And of course, that includes me as well.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: All righty, time to hop back into the driver's cabin!

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Uhh... are you listening to me? Umm, I just want to remind everyone that...

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: ...Every year, three hundred thousand people suffer fractures aboard transport vehicles for various reasons, fifteen thousand of which are attributed to bottletrees tipping over in transit.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: *sigh*...

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Just ignore him. I'll start the water pump slowly so there's no risk of falling off the tree.

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: But, accidents always happen...

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Alright, I'm starting 'er up! Hold on tight, Potlid!

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Every year–– Every year, there are a thousand more people–– who die to tree trunks bending during sudden strong wind––

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: I did it, Lanns!

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: The pump's starting to hum as it drains the water out of the tree trunk! Heehee, I love when this happens!

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Hah, why else would I say I trust you?

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Umm, actually, there's a chance the water pump might explode as well...

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: What's your deal? Is that a death note you're holding or what?

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Every year, I hear about an old friend or two who ends up contracting Oripathy or gets caught up in a Catastrophe, regardless of what field they work in. No avoiding it. If we go by what you say, we're all better off not working in the first place.

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: S-Sorry... I just wanted to give you some... points of reference from my limited knowledge and experience. Just trying to help.

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: I, I... do marketing for an insurance company...

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: 'Insurance'?

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: It's the best thing I've seen advertised in years! I've already bought a bunch of policies, and hope to get this Columbian company's name out there.

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: But I... I'm a bit skittish, afraid of everything.

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: But there's insurance for everything I'm scared of, including dangers I had no idea even existed.

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Look, these are my notes... Data collected from several of our company's advertisements, telling you about all the dangers you wouldn't ever think of!

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Also, they promised to compensate me in the event that something actually does happen.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Cool. So, how do you plan to spend that money if you're dead? It'd be pretty cool if they invented a way to continue living after you die though.

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Uh, I'm afraid... there's not much we can do about that.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Then, what's the point?

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Listen up. You help dress the vehicle up, and we'll take it on over to the nearby nomadic platform. Need to check if a buddy of mine is home.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: How many vehicles run into Catastrophes each year, and where? Doesn't mean shit to me. I'll just ask her straight up for a safe route to the Grinning Valley safely, and that'll be the end of things.

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Ugh... How'd we even get to this point?

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: I thought the little girl would just hide quietly in the vehicle, so all I had to do was squeeze into a tool room with her. Felt like the safest thing at the time...

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: ...But then she wanted to go visit friends and relatives with Alanna, leaving me alone in the vehicle.

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Here I am... alone in a hijacked transport harboring Infected people, forced to work, getting shot at with rocket launchers more than once!

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: I-I-I-I can't handle these people chasing me!

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: So, I don't care who it is, who I have to follow. Just don't make me deal with this whole mess alone...

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Th-Th-Th-This is all the m-m-money in my wallet. Here, take the whole thing! Please!

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: I, I never said I wasn't willing to follow you! I mean, it's only natural to not want to be a hostage, right...?

steps.name: Ray
steps.text: Hostage?

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: I, I get it. You're the jacker, so if I go with you, I'll end up a hostage. But, you were so cool when you saved those people, like a real highwayman...

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: ...Th-That's not what I meant! I'm just trying to say you're really impressive!

steps.name: Ray
steps.text: ...Me? Impressive?

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Wh-Why yes, that's right...

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Umm... You're not mad, are you? Thank goodness.

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Um, there is one thing I wanted to ask you. Alanna let you leave to buy the supplies we need to make the long-distance trip... So, can we just do it like that and not resort to robbing people?

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: See, I've even given you my wallet now. There might not be much money in there, but it should be enough to cover food and fuel...

steps.name: Ray
steps.text: Alright.

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Phew... That's a relief.

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Oh, right. Something was rubbing me the wrong way. You know how the men at the checkpoint were looking at us funny?

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: I'm a professional. Do you think... that we're already under suspicion?

steps.name: Ray
steps.text: It's just – I never said I wanted to take a hostage. I said anyone who wanted to get off was free to go.

steps.name: Ray
steps.text: Why don't you go?

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Umm... Huh? I thought I told you before...

steps.name: Ray
steps.text: I want to go to the Grinning Valley. That has nothing to do with you.

steps.name: Ray
steps.text: It's a long and dangerous journey, and I knew that going in. Which is why I gave you the chance to hop off.

steps.name: Ray
steps.text: You're scared of danger, so why are you still here?

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Well, since you're such a nice person, would you mind coming with me to have a look at the newsstand?

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: I can explain...

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: No... Normally, this wouldn't be...

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Ray, my face is hidden by the newspaper, isn't it?

steps.name: Ray
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Okay, now let's take a good look here...

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: ...Phew. Great, I haven't made it onto the list of missing persons yet.

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Though, uh, even if they did realize someone was missing, it wouldn't make it into the papers within a single day...

steps.name: Ray
steps.text: What about wanted persons?

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Not seeing anything––

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: It, it isn't what you think!

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: I just...

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: ...skipped out on my marriage.

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Well, it's not that I got cold feet. I was taking this transport, on my way to attend my engagement ceremony in another city, when you hijacked it...

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: But then... I realized I was pretty happy about that.

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Heh. Though, I guess that isn't some big deal either. And because it's not a big deal, I'm kind of embarrassed to talk about it...

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: I dunno how it is with your family, but in my case, I've got thirty-six brothers and sisters, and lots of other relatives... So you find plenty of stuff ends up not worth talking about...

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Alright, so maybe you don't get it. I also know there are lots of people with huge families that don't deal with this sort of thing.

steps.name: Ray
steps.text: Sorry, can't help you with that one...

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: ...Hold on, Ray. There are uniformed men coming this way. The same as the last checkpoint...

steps.name: Ray
steps.text: I didn't grow up in a big family.

steps.name: Ray
steps.text: Those houses, all joined together neatly, looked so beautiful. But, I didn't know where I ought to settle myself down.

steps.name: Ray
steps.text: The Zalak's gone.

steps.name: Ray
steps.text: Hm, he probably decided to leave on his own. Should've hopped off to begin with.

steps.name: Uniformed Worker
steps.text: Good day, ma'am. We'd like to have a little chat with you.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Don't be scared, Potlid. The pictures on the wall might be a bit spooky, but the lady here isn't into anything too weird.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: She takes pictures of giant beast carcasses in the primordial forest, plus the bones of explorers in the morass, but she's never hurt anybody.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Haha, well, at least, she probably wouldn't hurt anyone.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Huh. You're not even talking back when I call you Potlid. Where'd your spirit go? You hungry or something?

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Dunno if we can count on the jacker at all, but hopefully she manages to bring the stuff back without any issues. I'll show you a neat hack later – you can use solar panels to fry up some instant noodle cakes and fowlbeast eggs!

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: ...Put the past behind you.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Anyways, I have a solution now. Doesn't the jacker seem odd to you? Maybe even... a bit crazy? That's why I decided to meet this friend and ask her about the situation.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: A shadow as tall as a mountain? And it can talk? If a thing like that really exists in Rim Billiton, my friend surely would've heard of it.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: But, if the jacker simply had too much to drink, or went into the mines without a helmet and hit her head, well... I'll have to figure something else out.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Don't worry. They don't call me 'Alanna of the Barrenlands' for nothing. I'll always figure something out.

steps.name: Asbestos
steps.text: Get lost, and be quick about it. I'm busy with my travel notes. Didn't you see the sign on the door?

steps.name: Asbestos
steps.text: ––Wait, not many know about my temporary studio in the first place. Which rag do you work for? And how'd you manage to track me down?

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Lanns... Didn't you say you were old friends? She doesn't seem to... recognize you.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Haha, well... the 'old' part means we haven't seen each other in a long time.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Hey, remember that time we went down to Big Hammer Mine? There was that one manglerbeast trying to tear us apart. Reckon that was the biggest manglerbeast known to man?

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Right, right, it's the one on the wall there! I was behind the wheel when you took this photo.

steps.name: Asbestos
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Asbestos
steps.text: Alright... I don't care who you are or what you want, but I'll give you ten minutes. Don't test my patience.

a.text: Sorry to occupy your precious time, but I have to vent a bit – this is the single darkest day I've ever suffered.

Of course, I know that 'you' don't actually exist; I've just gotten used to having someone to talk to ever since I was little. After all, there were always so many people talking at once back home, and I... had the faintest voice.
Anyways, all I wanted to say was... it's way too dark under this truck.

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: (Patience, now. Just five more seconds. Wait for the shoes to go out of sight...)

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: (Four... three... two... one...)

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: *cough*, *cough* *cough*! ...Blurgh!

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Ugh... At least two mouthfuls of dirt won't send me to the hospital, even if this is the dried sand on the chassis we're talking about...

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Alright, I can feel it. This should be the access door leading to the power room on the bottom level.

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: It's too scary to walk around outside, so I squeezed back inside the vehicle to wait for them to return...

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Though... I'm not sure if Ray's gonna be coming back... I feel bad leaving her behind like that, but it's not like I did it on purpose.

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: One, two––

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Finally, the valve opened!

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Oh no! S-S-S-Sorry! I got in the wrong vehicle!

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: I'll be leaving now...

steps.name: Voice Outside the Vehicle
steps.text: Hold it.

steps.name: Voice Outside the Vehicle
steps.text: I hear something coming from under the vehicle.

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Oh no...

steps.name: Strange Lady
steps.text: Shh—

steps.name: Strange Lady
steps.text: (whispers) Quiet down.

steps.name: Strange Lady
steps.text: (whispers) If you blow my cover, nothing good's going to come of it.

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: (Nods in silence)

steps.name: Voice Outside the Vehicle
steps.text: We can't afford to let those damned metal crabs crawl into the station anymore! The last time one got in, it totaled three vehicles, and shanked two people to boot!

steps.name: Voice Outside the Vehicle
steps.text: Go grab a torch. I need to take a look.

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: (Gestures wildly in despair)

steps.name: Strange Lady
steps.text: (whispers) Come out.

steps.name: Ray
steps.text: Yeah, I got these coupons from somebody else. I don't know much about your market here.

steps.name: Uniformed Worker
steps.text: Then why the hell are you answering our market research questions?!

steps.name: Ray
steps.text: Because you asked them.

steps.name: Uniformed Worker
steps.text: Ugh, alright then. I guess we have to throw out that whole transcript. Sorry for bothering you, ma'am.

steps.name: Ray
steps.text: No worries.

steps.name: Ray
steps.text: 'Monthly promo magazine, clip this for 10% off compressed canned food.'

steps.name: Ray
steps.text: When did this kind of stuff start showing up?

steps.name: Ray
steps.text: Alanna is pretty incredible. She's got all the little details worked out in life, everything down the list.

steps.name: Ray
steps.text: 'On Friday, go grab a scarf from the old man with a stuffed tail, and get a friends discount from his daughter.' Yeah. She's got everything figured out, down to the day.

steps.name: Ray
steps.text: This stack of papers can be used in the Three Million Trolleys supermarket, and this stack...
That's right, Doctor. Actually, even my own memory is a bit fuzzy.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: It's as if Rim Billiton has always been like this. Rusty factories, steel frames stacked on top of each other, a gray skyscape, and Originium clusters towering in the horizon...

steps.name: Savage
steps.text: Sorry, Amiya. I really would like for you to be able to go home and have a good look around... I was looking for your parents for a long while.

steps.name: Savage
steps.text: But after the attack on the engineering team, the nomadic plate you used to live on got dismantled. The place we're standing right now probably has the most stuff from the old plate.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: No worries, Savage. This is enough. Thank you so much.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Just smelling the rust, oil, and welding rods is bringing back memories.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: It's as if... I've gone back in time.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Oh, what am I even saying...? It's only been a few years.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: It's just... I can still feel myself sitting in the back of a construction truck, following my parents and the other folks on the engineering team, waiting for them to set out from the plate.

steps.name: Savage
steps.text: It's a common practice in many large families.

steps.name: Savage
steps.text: The household oftentimes IS the engineering team. If the team has to go work in some faraway place, they'll take the old and the young with them, to make sure they're taken care of.

steps.name: Savage
steps.text: Of course, not all the people in the family are necessarily blood-related. Sometimes, they'll be considered part of the household just by living in the same part of the factory.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Oh, Doctor, there's no need to feel bad for me... It's not like I was thinking about the accident.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: And besides, I'd already carefully thought through what I was searching for, even before I came to Rim Billiton.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Oh, Doctor, look over there! I still remember that smokestack...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Erm...

steps.name: Savage
steps.text: What's wrong, Amiya?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: ...I suddenly remembered challenging the other kids to see who could crawl down there the farthest while keeping their tails as clean as possible...

options: Sounds like fun. I'd like to give it a try.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: It was totally fine. None of us wanted to get scolded by the adults back home, so we never went too far down.

steps.name: Savage
steps.text: Crikey, when's the last time I heard Amiya talking like this?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I'm afraid you don't qualify, Doctor. You don't have a tail.

steps.name: Savage
steps.text: Crikey, when's the last time I heard Amiya talking like this?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I'm not the same six or seven-year-old kid I was back then either!

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: But, at last, I've found something I recognize.

steps.name: Savage
steps.text: This is still Rim Billiton after all.

steps.name: Savage
steps.text: It's how we build our houses. Old buildings are incredibly useful, so there's no need to dismantle them. If you want a new house, just build right on top of it.

steps.name: Savage
steps.text: Which is why the elders tell us from the time we're little...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: ...'Adventurous folk, no matter how far they travel, always know home when they come back to it.'

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: That being said, a lot of things have changed as well.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: For example, the Infected persons management law we just came across seems to be imitating Leithanien's legal framework and Victoria's jargon...

options: Someone's been staring at you for a while now.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Mmhmm. I've noticed, Doctor.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I don't think I've seen her before... Also, I don't think any of the people who took care of me before would recognize me now.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Let's keep moving, Doctor. I'm sure it's fine.

steps.name: Ray
steps.text: ...The coupon flyer and the shopping list to go with it have gotten all mixed up. Now, what did Alanna tell me to get again...?

steps.name: Asbestos
steps.text: So that's the whole deal. The stretch from Windy Beach to the Grinning Valley is the most Catastrophe-prone place, say the Messengers. I've seen it myself too.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Oh? What's so special about the place?

steps.name: Asbestos
steps.text: Well, you could say that its ecology is–

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Is what?

steps.name: Asbestos
steps.text: ––Devoid of fowlshit.

steps.name: Asbestos
steps.text: Though Billy's natural geography is generally pretty barren to begin with, this area is SO barren that you won't even find fowlbeast droppings.

steps.name: Asbestos
steps.text: You want an 'easy' route? Not even in your dreams. If you want a road paved for you, you can look towards the rocks raining from the sky.

steps.name: Asbestos
steps.text: And don't expect to find anything fun to do either. All you find is the usual Billy stuff – ready to kill at the drop of a hat.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Alright, so other than the fowlbeasts that don't poop, any other special creatures to look out for?

steps.name: Asbestos
steps.text: Other creatures? Well, there's a scary number of sandbeasts. And listen to me here, you don't want anything to do with them. They'll mess you up!

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Sure, sure. Got it. Sandbeasts. Nothing unusual about those.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Isn't there anything a bit more... 'talkative,' 'shining,' 'incredibly huge,' anything along those lines?

steps.name: Asbestos
steps.text: How would I know? I'm not even a professional explorer, let alone a cryptid biologist.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: C'mon, don't be in such a rush to shoo us away...

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Lemme just ask you one last time.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: 'Rays of light.' 'A shadow as tall as a mountain.' 'Talking.' These words don't mean anything to you, right?

steps.name: Asbestos
steps.text: ––Say that again, one more time?

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Rays of light. A shadow as tall as a mountain. Talks.

steps.name: Asbestos
steps.text: Nah, yeah. That's a thing.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Asbestos
steps.text: *sigh*... What a pain. In the end, I really did remember something for your sake.

steps.name: Asbestos
steps.text: (Sargonian) 'Feranmut.'

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: What language is that?

steps.name: Asbestos
steps.text: Sargonian. Course, not many know the word to begin with.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Huh. Where's Sargonia?

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: I mean, that doesn't matter here. You should be using your precious time to tell me what that word means.

steps.name: Asbestos
steps.text: Huh? Didn't you hear what I just said? Almost nobody knows the word at all!

steps.name: Asbestos
steps.text: So, I've got no way of explaining it. Anything would just come out silly. Nobody's ever really studied exactly what a Feranmut is; it's just a vague concept that I happened to hear about.

steps.name: Asbestos
steps.text: Forget it, just act like you never heard anything from me. Don't even think about it, and certainly don't go throwing that word around. Nothing irks my tail more than fake news getting spread all over the place. I just end up running around for nothing.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Alright, alright. I'll forget you ever said anything.

steps.name: Asbestos
steps.text: Don't need your thanks or your words of praise. Your ten minutes are up, and the door is thataway. Are we clear?

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Yeah, clear as day.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Although... I'm still going to thank you anyway. The first bit you said, that this is a thing, that's good enough for me.

steps.name: Asbestos
steps.text: ...Hmph.

steps.name: Asbestos
steps.text: Rays of light? Shadows as tall as mountains? Feranmuts?

steps.name: Asbestos
steps.text: Who the hell would believe anything so crazy?

steps.name: Asbestos
steps.text: These made-up legends are growing out of control. People really oughta stop trying to mess with me.

steps.name: Asbestos
steps.text: Ugh...

steps.name: Asbestos
steps.text: How about... I finish these goddamn investigation reports and head on over to the Grinning Valley to take a look?

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Whaddya think?

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: If you're planning on going, then of course you have my full support! Even though I don't know anything about exploring or archaeology, there has to be some way I can help!

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Huh? Nah, I was asking how you felt about getting kicked out after ten minutes.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Didn't you tag along so I wouldn't lose track of time chatting with my old friend? Looks like I didn't need your supervision.

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: That's true, heehee.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: You know, when you really can't muster a smile... you don't have to force yourself. Even just a bit.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: If you're tired and want to vent, I'll make sure nobody sees you.

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Aaaaaaaaaaaaahhhh! I finally found a nice tunnel I can hide in! I'm saved!

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Strange Lady
steps.text: Hurry. Get your rear in there.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: As a friendly reminder, the left side's the sewage pipeline of the scalecis processing factory. I'd hop over to the other side, if I were you.

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Thanks a million, Alanna!

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Oh, wait. Fancy running into you here.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: (Raises an eyebrow)

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Um... I can explain...

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: I think someone's seen through our disguise and is setting up near the checkpoint. Ray seems to have gotten herself tangled up, but... I'm sure she has a way out.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Just a sec. The people chasing you are after us because of what we've done?

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Uhh, I'm not too sure about that...

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: I, I mean, my thing definitely doesn't matter!

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: I just happened to be hiding in the wrong place, so I got caught up in this Keira's mess again...

steps.name: Strange Lady
steps.text: Grab the rope, Jerry!

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Y-Yeah! Got it – I'll help you throw the knot over, and then you can lower me down!

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: ...In any case, that's the situation, Alanna. Don't worry about me! Gotta run for now!

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Did he actually get himself involved, or is he just running because he happened to see someone else running?

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: But y'know, Potlid, don't you the one next to him looks kinda familiar?

a.text: Life really is terrifying. And you can't run away from it, no matter how much you might want to... Well, actually, I've never wanted to run away.

I always went with the flow, safely and securely, along with my thirty-six other siblings and the other three hundred thousand people in the city. After all, you naturally gravitate towards whatever's the most stable.
But I got attacked out of nowhere. I ended up skipping out on my engagement, and now I'm actually on the run with my very own two feet.
I don't know why, but, even as I'm being chased by all sorts of things and running for my life....
––In the end, a door always opens for me.

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: *pant*, *pant*... Are things getting better or worse for us?

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Logically speaking, if there's a nest of metal crabs beneath the sewer, we ought to contact a security officer. That's what it says under the 'beware of wildlife' signs...

steps.name: Strange Lady
steps.text: Bad news is, we just barged straight into their home in our attempt to escape.

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Ha... Ahaha...

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: I can't feel my lungs anymore...

steps.name: Strange Lady
steps.text: Don't slow down now! Unless you want to end cut to ribbons by those pincers!

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: I, I really can't deal with this whole running away thing...

steps.name: Strange Lady
steps.text: Do I come across as some career criminal who's constantly on the run? I'm just...

steps.name: Strange Lady
steps.text: ...I just wanted people to think I went missing, so I crawled into the bed of my hardware store's delivery truck and went to sleep for a day.

steps.name: Strange Lady
steps.text: Then, the cargo box ended up getting transported away as usual and I found myself waking up in someone else's vehicle...

steps.name: Strange Lady
steps.text: And here we are.

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: You're not a career criminal? Thank goodness, I thought I saw your face somewhere before on a wanted poster.

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Oh, b-but I don't mean to say that you look generic or ordinary...

steps.name: Strange Lady
steps.text: You know, I've had a question my mind. You really went and helped someone you thought was a wanted criminal?

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: I, I just felt like I had no choice... From the very beginning, I didn't know why those men were even chasing me...

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: ...Plus, I think you're actually a good egg. Same as the ladies who abducted me and brought me here. They're actually pretty decent...

steps.name: Strange Lady
steps.text: Ugh! So loud...

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Hold on, where are we...?

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: ...I've got an idea!

steps.name: Strange Lady
steps.text: Let's hear it.

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Huh? You're letting me call the shots? Th-This is rather new for me...

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: ...Long story short, that sound's the smelting plant's automatic waste filtration and disposal system. I've seen someone falling off it in one of our company ads, he suffered a terrible fracture...

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: ...My point is, if people can fall from it, that also means there has to be a way up. We might be able to climb on top of that thing.

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: There's no way the metal crabs could chase us up that high! And our pursuers would never expect us to leave the factory. Let's go this way!

steps.name: Strange Lady
steps.text: You want us to walk across these... rickety platforms that look like they could flip over at a moment's notice? Along these iron slabs that could easily send us flying?

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: It's not completely impossible! The robotic arms are on a timer! I'll climb up first and look for the control room. It'll be safe, as long as I manually operate the arms!

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: I saw Alanna driving the transport. The operating lever for this mechanical platform should be just like that vehicle's shifter...

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: I might be able to pull this off... I just need to give it a shot...

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: I mean... I can't say for sure if it's going to work or not, but...

steps.name: Strange Lady
steps.text: I trust you. You can do it. Just go for it.

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: You trust me? Wait... Not only are you willing to let me call the shots, but you're also placing your faith in me? Dear lord... not one of my thirty-six siblings has ever dared...

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: But, you're also smart and independent, just like them––

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Um, I'm sorry, Keira... But, the platform's taller than I expected... I can't reach... Could you give me a little boost?

steps.name: Strange Lady
steps.text: A boost? Like this...? Here?

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Th-Th-That works too, b-but I was kind of thinking my back or legs or...

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Woah, you're strong! Great, I made it up!

steps.name: Strange Lady
steps.text: Awesome...

steps.name: Strange Lady
steps.text: (Whispers) And you're nothing like the elders constantly trying to dictate my life.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: So what you're saying is, nobody's on to us, and nobody's tracking us.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: You didn't kill anyone with this, did you?

steps.name: Ray
steps.text: Yeah, nah. There were so many things on your shopping list, I didn't have a free hand to draw my weapon.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Alright, as long as you didn't cause any trouble.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: *sigh*... I've had more than my fair share of excitement. That incident at the checkpoint was already hard enough on Potlid.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Where'd our resident coward go?

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: We... Phew, we're finally safe. We actually did it...

steps.name: Strange Lady
steps.text: Thank you. I really mean that. Thank you so much.

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Haha... My timid heart's still ready to jump out of my ribcage... I, I actually followed through with a decision? And such a dangerous one at that?

steps.name: Strange Lady
steps.text: Quit bashing yourself over the head with your briefcase already. People are staring.

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Ugh, sorry... It's just that, I'm a lot more used to going along with other people's plans. I had a big family, and things got pretty loud...

steps.name: Strange Lady
steps.text: Yeah, I get you. Most people are pretty much the same. Everyone joins in, and things get noisy, whether or not they're actually blood-related.

steps.name: Strange Lady
steps.text: It's been a good decade since one of my sisters went out to travel across the lands, and a lot of the others don't even remember that she left Rim Billiton.

steps.name: Strange Lady
steps.text: What I'm trying to say is, it's perfectly normal to be forgotten, just as it's perfectly normal for twenty or thirty people to suddenly remember you at once and start talking about the same things on repeat.

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Haha, how right you are...

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: You know, I skipped out on my engagement today, which is how I ended up out here. It's also why I'm so afraid of getting caught.

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Well, actually, the whole thing was foisted onto me because of a little dust-up... But afterwards, I realized that I was pretty happy to be getting out of that marriage.

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: It hadn't dawned upon me until then that I was really against the whole arrangement!

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: I don't even know the first thing about the woman I'm engaged to! I just felt like... so many smart people in the family said I should do it, so it had to be the right thing!

steps.name: Strange Lady
steps.text: Right? I totally get you! The elders in my family always try to push their experiences onto me, and I got so sick and tired of their nagging that I wanted to disappear!

steps.name: Strange Lady
steps.text: Even though I left the old factories and went to Carrot's to an assembly line, they still packed themselves into a transport for a solid half day just to tell me that they 'found me a proper man.'

steps.name: Strange Lady
steps.text: If I'd gone along with it, then I would've missed everything that happened today...

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Um...

steps.name: Strange Lady
steps.text: ...It's nothing. You go ahead.

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Um... Keira, I'm just thinking, the two of us have a pretty good rapport... And, uh, my company recently rolled out a new insurance plan with really broad coverage...

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: I don't know if you'd be interested or not, but...

steps.name: Strange Lady
steps.text: Huh? Insurance? I'd be glad to help you with your work, since I do owe you one for today... But, what kind of insurance are we talking about here? And how much does it cost?

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: N-N-N-No, Miss Keira, that's not what I meant... It won't cost you any money. I just wanted to ask...

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: ...How would you feel about becoming the beneficiary of this insurance plan I just bought?

steps.name: Strange Lady
steps.text: ...Beneficiary?

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: I-I-In other words, if anything happens to me, then the company will pay you a large sum of money... As for the specific terms, I can go over the details with you, if you have time...

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: After all, a beneficiary is someone very important to me...

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Goodness, what's gotten into me?! Am I making decisions for myself again? And I swear, this has to be the most important decision of my life!

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Keira?

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: I know, this is all very sudden, but it's how I really feel, I just had to blurt it out...

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: The old me would've just kept it bottled up in my heart, thinking over and over about how to get the words out, and if I did get them out, worrying if I stuttered or not. Huh? Am I not stuttering anymore...?

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Oh! It's no big deal though... If you don't want to, then... Maybe I shouldn't have sprung it on you like that... Maybe, I...

steps.name: Strange Lady
steps.text: I'll do it.

steps.name: Strange Lady
steps.text: It's more in line with my personal principals than going along with whatever the elders have planned for me.

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Really...? You're fine with it? Oh my god! I really have to tell my siblings that I'm not going to let them lead me around by the nose forever.

steps.name: Strange Lady
steps.text: Totally. They're always going on about how they've been through so much and know better... My whole family's got a suite of rules when it comes to who we marry.

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Like how everyone loves a Cautus with long ears.

steps.name: Strange Lady
steps.text: Huh? Cautus?

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Ah, yes. I'm the only Zalak in the family. I guess I got handed off to this family when I was little.

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: I forget about that a lot, same as people forget about me. Besides... what big family isn't cobbled together like this?

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Ah, and they like loud talkers.

steps.name: Strange Lady
steps.text: My relatives are more into the quiet types.

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: And industrious, businessy types.

steps.name: Strange Lady
steps.text: Who know how to make a sales pitch.

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Even their appearance...

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Wait...

steps.name: Somewhat Familiar Woman
steps.text: ...You just mentioned that you were skipping out on an engagement ceremony, didn't you?

steps.name: Potlid
steps.text: Lanns, if we don't leave now, we'll be surrounded by drivers bringing wine barrels over to collect bottletree water, and won't be able to get out...

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: I know that already.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Seriously, didn't that Zalak say he was scared to death that something terrible would happen as soon as he left the vehicle?

steps.name: Ray
steps.text: I told him everyone's free to get off whenever they want, and I wouldn't do anything to stop him.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Naw, the way he was talking, I think he was scared he'd run into the girl he was engaged to.

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: Ray! Alanna! Hurry up and give me your contact!

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Jerry
steps.text: I'll send you the details later! Wedding invitations!

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: ...Huh?

steps.name: Ray
steps.text: As far as I can tell, the road ahead should be pretty safe. No traces of big beasties, no sign of the ground getting hollowed out by the wildlife.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Haha. Maybe that last blessing the Zalak left you is actually doing something for us after all.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: 'Have a safe trip,' and 'you'll definitely find what you're looking for.'

steps.name: Ray
steps.text: 'Feranmut,' huh...?

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Pretty tough, just going by the sound of that word, huh? If you walked up to me and told me, 'we're going to go find the Feranmut,' I wouldn't have questioned it for a moment.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Though, I didn't think you'd also read the road conditions.

steps.name: Ray
steps.text: Hardly. I don't have much experience, I'm not a real lookout.

steps.name: Ray
steps.text: I just think... looking out into the distance with binoculars is pretty neat, that's all.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: ––Weird.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: The power system's temperature display seems a bit off.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Jacker, did we miss something just now?

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Like, a geyser spewing steam by the side of the road, or active Originium on the surface causing a small-scale explosion?

steps.name: Ray
steps.text: Nope.

steps.name: Ray
steps.text: I made sure of it.

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: What about Potlid?

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Where'd she get herself to while we were looking outside?

steps.name: Alanna
steps.text: Wait, is she... in the power room?!
